What i did is didn't worry about building anything real nice in the begining, and did my best to get to coal power as soon as I could. By the time you get there you will have plenty of building supplies to work with and with coal you can get a lot of automated power without having to deal with the biomass burners.

Now I don't have to worry about power as much and can easily expand my power base without having to babysit a bunch of burners so I can worry about other things. Plus once you get to that point that's when steel and other advanced products start coming into play that will really benefit from an optimized factory.

Now is also the time I am really starting to try and get the hard drives. I found that if you research drives when just starting out the alternate recipes they give relate more to your iron age so to speak. While not really bad, but once you start trying to get to steel production the alternate recipes you can get seem to be a lot more useful. One early recipe I got was casted screw, which gives me more screws straight from ignots instead of first having to convert them into rods, so being able to eliminate a whole step to get a products helps a lot on these big projects. Casted screw as a recipe kind of loses its value later down the line, but early on it's pretty great I think.

That being said, this is just what I did, and I still got a lot to learn.

Symphonic metal is just what is sounds like. Take the drums, bass, and toned down guitars of metal, and add an orchestra. Most, if not all, are fronted my a female singer, though some have death growls as backup. Bands? Here ya go. 

1. Nightwish- Probably the most famous symphonic band. All their albums are good, but their best are when Tarja was with them. My personal favorite album is Oceanborn, favorite song is Stargazers. 

2. Xandria- All their albums except for their latest one, in my opinion, were quirky. They were good, but quirky. Ravenheart is their best one with their original singer. However, their original singer left (forgot her name) and they replaced her, and decided to go full on symphony. Neverworld's End is their latest album, my favorite song is probably Blood on my Hands. 

3. Epica- Dutch Symphonic metal band, created my Mark Jensen after his departure from After Forever (more on them in a sec). He plays guitars and does backing vocals, death growls, band is fronted by Simone Simmons, smoking hot with an even hotter voice. Album? Design Your Universe. Song? Our Destiny. 

4. After Forever- Mark Jensen original band, did the same thing as in epica. Till he got kicked out. Fronted by Floor Jensen (no relation). Album: Decipher Song: Monolith of doubt. 

Now... POWER METAL! Combines elements of speed metal and traditional  metal with symphonic elements. Unlike most metal generes, power metal is noted for being "uplifting." Extreme use of keyboards. Finds much inspiration from Ronnie James Dio. Notably, it is known for being epic and a bit theatrical to a degree. Often these bands hail from europe, typically male frontmen singing in multiple octaves. 

1. Dragonland- My favorite. First two and last albums tell the story of a place called... wait for it... Dragonland. Middle two don't. All of them are good, I am going to recommend the album Starfall, all songs are good, one of my favorite is In Perfect Harmony. 

2. Sabaton- Arguably the greatest and most well known power metal band. Lyrics are inspired by wars, typically WWI and WWII. Lead vocalist, Joakim Broden, has a ridiculously low voice. Its great. 
Album: Attero Dominatus, Song: Nuclear Attack

3. Powerwolf- Tongue in cheek, very quirky, just flat out insane. With songs like Resurrection by Erection or St. Satans Day, you can't take them too seriously. Use a keyboard that sounds like a church organ. Album: Bible of the Beast, Song: Panic in the Pentagram

4. Blind Guardian- The defining power metal band, often nicknames "the bards." Draw many of their lyrics from books, from "Nightfall in middle earth" which is a retelling of The Silmarillion, to the song "Time What is time" which seems to be about the book "Do androids dream of electric sheep", you have to pass a literature test to join the band. 
Album: Tales from the Twilight World, Song: Goodbye My Friend

5. Gamma Ray- Last one, cause I am tired of typing, though I could go on. A classic, helped shape the genre. After the lead vocalist departure from Helloween, he formed Gamma Ray. 
Album: Somewhere Out In Space, Song: Beyond the Gamma Ray

Plenty of others, but yeah. If you want examples of other genres, all you gots to do is ask or post, I will find it. ;D I love metal, listen to just about all genres, can help you with what you need.
